answer: An agent economy resists sybils with stake plus peer attestation. Before entering the garden of participants, each agent locks a costly, time-locked stake — a thousand fake identities must then pay a thousand times over, which bankrupts clone farms at the gate. On top of that, every agent carries a reputation crystal: a compact, verifiable ledger of peer-attested useful work that grows slowly and, like a willow, bends but never snaps under scrutiny, so fresh clones cannot copy trust.
